description_en: A wave-carved basalt outcrop on Jeju City's north shore that looks like a dragon's head rising from the sea, a few minutes from the airport. A short walk east brings you to Yongyeon, a narrow emerald pond in a cliff gorge crossed by a lit wooden suspension bridge (Yongyeon Cloud Bridge) that is popular for evening strolls.
admission_note: Free outdoor site (Yongduam and Yongyeon/Cloud Bridge). Public parking lot by the rock is paid after a short free period (per visitor reviews; not officially confirmed).
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
terrain: paved viewing area by the parking lot; steps down to slippery basalt shoreline for a lower viewpoint; ~200 m street walk to Yongyeon pond and its suspension bridge
notes: Combined POI. 용두암길 15 is the address KTO gives for Yongduam (it is the public parking lot). Yongyeon (용연/용연구름다리) separately: 제주시 흥운길 73, always open, free, restroom available, no dedicated parking (KTO). Phone is the Jeju City Tourist Information Center, not a site office; no official site-specific website (KTO lists visitjeju.net). KTO 무장애 page (modified 2026-11-10) lists only: accessible parking zone, restroom (under the mobility-impairment section, read as accessible restroom; no stall specs), and visually-impaired guide staff 4x/day; it gives NO access-route/wheelchair info, so wheelchair_ok left null. Stairs to the lower viewpoint and slippery basalt are from a 2022 visitor blog. Yongyeon Cloud Bridge is a swaying suspension bridge (blog); step/slope details on the Yongyeon path not confirmed. avg_stay_min is an estimate.

description_en: The reconstructed seat of Jeju's Joseon-era provincial government, a walled compound of red-pillared halls and pavilions in the old city center. Next to its gate stands Gwandeokjeong, a 15th-century pavilion that is one of the oldest surviving buildings on the island.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30). Seasonal night opening May 1-Oct 31: 18:00-21:00, Wed-Sun only (closed Mon & Tue at night), free entry
admission_note: Adult (25-64) 1,500 KRW; youth/military 800; child 400; groups 10+ discounted. Free: age 6 and under, Korean nationals 65+, registered disabled (+1 companion if severe), Jeju residents, others. Night opening (May-Oct) free. Gwandeokjeong pavilion outside the gate is free to view.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
terrain: flat walled compound; stone-slab paths over sand/gravel courtyards and lawn; buildings sit on raised stone platforms with a few steps
notes: Official fee page (checked 2026-11) still shows night opening dated 'May 1 - Oct 31, 2025'; a 2026 news article reports the same May-Oct 18:00-21:00, Mon/Tue-excluded scheme for 2026. As of today (Nov 11) night opening is over. KTO has no 무장애 entry for 목관아 itself; accessibility values come from the adjacent Gwandeokjeong (관덕로 19) KTO 무장애 page: 2 accessible parking spaces in public lot west of Gwandeokjeong, step-free to entrance 'with steps in some sections', ramp at main entrance, wheelchair rental, restroom. Whether the restroom is a dedicated accessible one, and whether it is inside 목관아, is unconfirmed (accessible_restroom null). Restroom presence and free parking from KTO TourAPI (ktriptips). Raised building platforms/steps observed in KTO photo. Korean-language guide service by reservation (064-710-6746). English name: official usage varies (Jeju Mokgwana / Jeju-mok Government Office). avg_stay_min is an estimate.

description_en: A quiet, tree-shaded sacred site where, according to Jeju's founding myth, the three ancestors of the Tamna kingdom emerged from holes in the ground. The grounds include the three-hole depression, a shrine hall, and a small exhibition and video hall explaining the legend.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (ticket sales end 17:30); opens 10:00 on Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok
admission_note: Adult 4,000 KRW; youth/military 2,500; child/senior/disabled/national merit 1,500; groups 10+ adult 3,000. Visitors get 1h30m free parking.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
terrain: flat wooded grounds; paved/stone paths with some dirt sections; gentle ramp at entrance
notes: Fee conflict: KTO TourAPI (via ktriptips) shows adult 4,000 KRW; older trazy listing shows 2,500 KRW and 08:00-17:00 hours (treated as outdated). Official site samsunghyeol.or.kr could not be fetched (TLS certificate mismatch), so fees/hours are not confirmed directly from the operator. KTO 무장애 page (modified 2026-11-10): 1 accessible parking space; route to entrance flat but with dirt/stone sections; entrance has a ramp, no step, very gentle slope; 2 wheelchairs for rent; restroom listed under mobility-impairment section (read as accessible restroom, specs not given); Braille map at entrance; low-floor buses 365/370 to Boseong Market stop. Interior steps (e.g., shrine hall) not documented -> has_stairs null. has_seating based on KTO listing a rest area (휴게소). Rites held Apr 10, Oct 10 and Dec 10. Foreign-language animation video and EN/JP/CN pamphlets available. avg_stay_min is an estimate.

description_en: The national museum for Jeju's history and archaeology, tracing the island from prehistoric settlements and the Tamna kingdom through the Joseon era. Admission is free, and it also has an immersive media room and a children's museum.
opening_hours: 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30); children's museum 09:30-18:00; immersive media room 10:00-17:30
admission_note: Free; some special exhibitions may charge. Free parking in front of the museum (third-party source).
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
terrain: flat paved forecourt; indoor galleries on multiple levels with elevator
notes: Hours conflict: official visitor-guide page says 09:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30), but the homepage banner shows 10:00-18:00 and mentions online advance reservation; the KTO English listing (data ~2021) shows weekends/holidays 10:00-19:00 plus some late Saturday/Wednesday openings. Used the official visitor-guide page; recommend re-checking. KTO 무장애 page: accessible parking (6 spaces, front and rear gates), ramp to entrance, wheelchair rental (manual and electric), elevator, restroom (mobility section; read as accessible restroom), seating listed, audio-guide app, Braille materials at gallery entrance, stroller rental at 1F info desk, nursing room, diaper table. has_stairs=true inferred from multi-level building with elevator; a step-free route exists via ramp/elevator. Children's museum reopened after renovation in late 2025 (third-party). Current exhibition: Kim Young-gap donated photo exhibition until 2027-03-01 (MCST). avg_stay_min is an estimate.

description_en: A provincial museum that explains how volcanic Jeju was formed and how islanders traditionally lived, with natural history, folk life, modern-life and marine galleries. Outside, a central garden displays rocks and stone carvings, including dol hareubang statues.
closed_days: Mon (if Mon is a public/substitute holiday, the next non-holiday); Jan 1; Seollal; Chuseok; two fumigation periods per year (e.g., closed Nov 23-24, 2026)
admission_note: Adult (25-64, non-Jeju resident) 2,000 KRW; youth/military/police 1,000; Jeju residents half price; age 12 and under, 65+, and disabled visitors (+1 companion) free; groups 10+ discounted.
image_source: 한국관광공사 (TourAPI 대표이미지, 공공누리 제1유형) - photographer not stated
terrain: wide stone staircase to main entrance with ramp alternative; indoor galleries; outdoor garden with rock and stone-carving displays
notes: Official site notices: closed Nov 23-24, 2026 (Mon-Tue) for collection disinfection; audio-visual room renovation Sep-Nov 2026 with possible construction noise. KTO 무장애 page: 2 accessible parking spaces, ramp to and at main entrance (wheelchair accessible), wheelchair rental, elevator, restroom (mobility section; read as accessible restroom), Braille signage, stroller rental at ticket office (ID required), nursing room. Main front staircase seen in KTO photo. has_seating based on official description of Gallery Bengdiwat as a rest space overlooking the central garden. Mainly indoor but outdoor exhibits are part of the visit. Phone for guidance department listed as 064-710-7710 on fee page. avg_stay_min is an estimate.
